speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; could you describe exactly where the lesions are located and how they appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Borrelia burgdorferi infection) with disseminated symptoms.

The combination of recent Minnesota camping, a prior self-resolving knee pain (likely early localized or early disseminated Lyme), and now wrist pain with fever and skin lesions is highly suggestive of Lyme arthritis or disseminated Lyme disease. I will request serology testing to confirm this.

REQUEST TEST: Lyme Serology (ELISA followed by Western Blot)
REQUEST TEST: CBC with Differential
REQUEST TEST: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate)
